contracts.semantic_clause:
### Mandatory generated-context verification

DI-01 — At bootstrap, conversation entry, adoption, relevant changed context and recovery, the runtime MUST verify the presence and integrity of both complete mandatory texts in the resolved generated workspace view against the deterministic representation supplied by its actually adopted distribution. During initial bootstrap, use the explicitly selected eligible initial target and record target verification separately; do not claim adoption before its existing gates pass. Resolve owned controller/source identity and checkpoint applicability before reliance; a shared checkout or self-declared identity cannot select another runtime's adopted rules.

DI-02 — This is a check of disposable workspace-generated output against its expected adopted-distribution rendering, NOT an audit of OOP repository/release contents, authenticity or file-to-commit correspondence. BOOT-03's repository, signature, hash, inventory, publisher and release-test exclusions remain binding; they do not prohibit this scoped comparison of local generated workspace instructions. Consumers use the distribution and MUST NOT read PROTOCOL.md for this procedure. A matching title, metadata comment, file presence, exit code or model declaration alone cannot pass.

DI-03 — Distinguish present-and-integral, missing, incomplete-or-altered, source-or-version-unavailable and verification-unavailable with actual observations. Require the single mandatory block to start at byte zero and compare its complete bytes, including source identity, timing, force and both texts. The layer-set identity is insufficient. On failure or uncertainty attempt only authorized reconstruction from the applicable source, preserve valid organization/workspace layers and unrelated instructions, conditionally replace owned derived content, read back actual bytes and reverify before reporting recovery. Keep failed attempts distinct from the verified result. If unavailable use an authorized alternative context path; block only work dependent on unavailable mandatory context.

DI-04 — Native pointer reconciliation MUST compare only the activation/preservation content and resolved locators from the adopted template, retaining documented host variations, necessity, placement, ownership, concurrency and existing authority. Remove superseded embedded copies from the owned block and preserve safe reference delivery. Preserve unrelated host content outside the owned activation block and never rewrite peer-owned files. Generation, configured delivery, observed delivery, application and verified outcomes MUST remain separately evidenced; no synthetic consumer dispatch or comprehension test is introduced.

### Context Integrity Attestation and selective rehydration

For adopted Core, Semantic Routing Index and applicable modules, context integrity MUST distinguish verified_loaded, reused_verified, stale, unknown and missing or equivalent states. Valid states require exact adopted release/source identity, artifact path/content identity, workspace/persistent-runtime/session scope and applicable request/action scope, checked evidence/time and lifecycle mechanism basis establishing availability. Remembered text, a historical load log, an unrelated checkpoint or schema validity alone cannot establish currently available normative context. A context attestation MAY remain transient; retain only continuity/verification evidence needed under existing private ownership rules.

Context compaction, truncation/reduction, recovery, new session, unverified reopen/resume, runtime/model replacement, workspace switch, OOP/module identity change, route change, material scope expansion, discovered risk/action class, capability topology change, handoff and stale/unknown attestation MUST invalidate affected context until its availability and identity are verified. Route expansion need not invalidate unchanged verified artifacts; loss of retention evidence invalidates every affected retained artifact. A workspace switch clears project-specific active context and cannot reuse another workspace's attestation.

For stale, unknown or missing context the runtime MUST selectively rehydrate the verified adopted Core when needed, current verified Semantic Routing Index, required module dependency closure, relevant canonical organizational facts and strictly necessary authorized private runtime facts. Check exact identities and lifecycle availability evidence before dependent effects; record loaded versus reused facts accurately. Always evaluating against current OOP does not mean rereading every byte every time. Uncertain retained normative context requires verified selective rehydration, never token-saving under-routing. No full fat-prompt reread is required per interaction. Adoption changes follow BOOT-03, compatibility, authorization and independent checkpoint gates without consumer repository/release verification.

Derived action context, when present, depends on applicable protocol identities, route/module closure, relevant organizational facts/revisions, authority, lifecycle phase and runtime capability topology. A materially changed dependency invalidates only affected derived instructions and evidence; reconstruct required context from verified sources before the dependent effect. Neither unchanged prompt bytes nor model recollection proves current underlying authority or state. Reuse still-valid context without compulsory per-tool-call recomposition, full-protocol rereads, remote polling or duplicate records.

### Context economy and retirement

Canonical OOP being available does not require the entire protocol to remain loaded in active model context. Maintain only the current semantic dependency closure and necessary evidence in the working set. Machine verification is not semantic reading: use available deterministic tools for hashes, inventory, equality, signatures, schema/version control state and deterministic invariants, retaining outcomes, identities and evidence references rather than reading every checked file into context. In the consumer lifecycle this applies to consumer project/runtime state and controls, not verification of the OOP repository or release; BOOT-03 governs that exclusion. Consumer runtimes MUST NOT read `PROTOCOL.md` during bootstrap, adoption, refresh or recovery: they read `dist/entry.json`, its minimum context and the routed closure, whose complete semantic clauses carry the canonical text. This never replaces a maintainer's mandatory complete semantic reading for a normative source change.

After context loss, use current action → reroute → dependency closure → exact evidence references → load only missing, stale or newly applicable context. Retire modules no longer needed for the next action while preserving necessary identity/evidence references; the working set SHOULD NOT grow monotonically merely because content was once read. Resume from valid bootstrap checkpoints and reuse unaffected evidence without losing any mandatory context/authority gate.

### R26 — Runtime guidance, declaration and local coordination

1. **Routing guidance.** The producer MUST derive, from reviewed module semantics traceable to complete source clauses, one compact runtime projection of the Semantic Routing Index: for every consumer module its id, an operational `use` statement written as recognizable request or action situations and the required response, and its selection facets; one fixed classification directive; and one index fingerprint. The projection is regenerable derived metadata, neither a module nor normative authority, and it MUST stay within a measured producer budget. Detail records MUST expose module-specific semantic conditions, preconditions and postconditions; identical generic text for every module does not satisfy the Semantic Routing Index requirement. The directive states: G0 means no governed mutation; technical_adoption alone creates no organizational records; for organizational work a work item is used only when the level requires it (G2+), a cited shared policy requires it, the user explicitly asks for it, it continues an existing one, or a stated continuity need requires it; classify and declare before creating it.
2. **Runtime-facing message.** Deliver additional context in this order: orientation, ticket reminder, working folder and retained chat history, current state and its modules, reachable states with consequences and modules, and any applicable synchronization and migration facts.
3. **Classification and state.** Derive conversation states from intake, inquiry, planning, execution, verification and recovery. Exclude bootstrap. At each prompt create a scoped turn; record actual classified level and ticket relation as attributed runtime claims. Load canonical module dependencies for the current and reachable states.
4. **Bounded history.** Persist only the turn reference, relevant classified state and safe structured routing facts for the owning installation and chat. Exclude raw prompts, secrets, transcripts and data from other chats. Limit retention and avoid exposing technical state in publication.
5. **Mandatory English reminder.** Classify every new subject. For organizational work above G1 unrelated to an existing ticket, immediately create, commit and push a new ticket within authority. Technical adoption alone stays in private technical state. Publish the updated state of a ticket under discussion whenever it changes significantly beyond a status-only change. Perform these effects only with actual capability and authority, verify their outcomes and report failures or unavailability accurately.
6. **Coordination.** Protect local shared synchronization and owned state with exclusive leases or equivalent coordination. Recheck state under coordination, reject stale writers and preserve recoverable state without changing path permissions.

7. **Orientation.** Instruct the runtime to use contextual guidance under OOP and apply the relevant modules. Actual authority and effects remain independently governed.
8. **Conversation transitions.** A new prompt returns to intake. A classified inquiry may lead to planning; a plan leads to authorized execution and outcome verification. Partial or uncertain effects lead to recovery. State updates must follow a reachable transition and match the current turn and expected revision.
9. **Migration.** On shared checkout synchronization deliver the selected revision and the applicable lifecycle and migration references. Execute applicable migration procedures before relying on the target rules. Advance the runtime’s independently verified adoption checkpoint only after actual applicable effects are verified.
